page: Microsoft Azure D96as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processors based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at speeds up to 4.5 GHz. It is provisioned with 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory footprint comprises 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction flags include AVX-512 extensions (such as AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic accelerators including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Across compute and throughput benchmarks, the instance yields top-tier metrics. Single-core stress-ng reaches 3,778.88 while multi-core stress-ng records 175,906.98. In PassMark tests, it achieves an overall CPU score of 117,071.49, complemented by high-ranking cryptographic and extended instruction marks. Memory subsystem evaluation demonstrates uncached large-block read throughput of 311.5 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 174.77 GB/sec, supporting rapid data handling across complex workloads.

Application tests reflect high parallel capacity, delivering 138.89 million operations per second in Redis SET testing and 92.8 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. In quantized CPU-based language model inference, text generation achieves 331.46 tokens/sec on 135M models, 59.5 tokens/sec on 7B models, and 6.74 tokens/sec on 70B models. The server includes no bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring attached network volumes for persistent storage needs.

This hardware profile delivers dense compute and memory throughput suitable for heavy multi-threaded enterprise workloads. Key fits include large relational and in-memory databases, large-scale static or API web serving, CPU-driven machine learning inference, and dense parallel data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D96as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors running up to 4.5 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) and 384.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Equipped with AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions, it achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng benchmarks and PassMark CPU testing. In application benchmarks, it reaches 138.89 million Redis SET operations per second and 92.8 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. It features no integrated GPUs and includes no local storage, relying on external network storage solutions. The hardware balance provides reliable compute density and large memory capacity well-suited for in-memory databases, distributed caching, web serving fleets, and large parallel data processing pipelines.
